test_title: PYST 42: SSC MTS 2024 - Numerical and Mathematical Ability (Held On: 30 Oct, 2024 - Shift 1)

question: The difference between the selling prices with 19% profit and 11% loss is Rs.454.50. What is the cost price of the item?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total difference in percentage = Profit % − (−Loss %) = 19% + 11% = 30%

Given that 30% of Cost Price = Rs. 454.50

⇒ 1% of Cost Price = 454.50 ÷ 30 = 15.15

⇒ 100% of Cost Price = 15.15 × 100 = 1515

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.1515.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit = 19%

Loss = 11%

Difference between Selling Prices = Rs. 454.50

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/254765f321fda04698d9d7ff3629cd2d3c09bb2b560159217c5a4e51bae5bca1.png] 

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the item be x.

Selling Price at 19% profit (SP₁) = x + 19% of x = 1.19x

Selling Price at 11% loss (SP₂) = x − 11% of x = 0.89x

According to the question, the difference in selling prices is Rs. 454.50:

⇒ SP₁ − SP₂ = 454.50

⇒ 1.19x − 0.89x = 454.50

⇒ 0.30x = 454.50

⇒ x = 454.50 ÷ 0.30

⇒ x = 1515

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.1515.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

CP is the price at which goods are bought. SP is the price at which goods are sold. Profit occurs when SP > CP, and Loss occurs when SP < CP.

Effective Change in Profit/Loss

When moving from a loss percentage to a profit percentage on the same base, the total change in percentage terms is the sum of both values (Profit % + Loss %).

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The fundamental relation between CP and MP is: MP × (100 − Discount %) = CP × (100 + Profit %).
